findings.title: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, which no longer exists
findings.body: `UsernamePasswordForm` now declares only `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`. `UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. No such overload exists in `UsernameForm` or `UsernamePasswordForm`, so the `services` module fails to compile. Pass `context.getUser()`, or restore a no-arg method, and make sure the semantics are what you intend for the username-only form.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are disabled for normal (non-re-auth) login
findings.body: The helper returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. It guards both `authenticate()` (line 115) and the error `challenge(...)` (line 137). The old code filled the WebAuthn data when `context.getUser() == null`, which is the ordinary login case. The new code fills it only when a user is already set, which is the re-authentication case. For a fresh login, and for the error page after an unknown username, no challenge, RP id or conditional-UI attribute is rendered. Discoverable-key and 'username webauthn' autocomplete login stops working, and the existing tests (`webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey`, `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`, `passwordLoginWithExternalKey`) would fail. The `user != null` condition should be dropped, or the helper should cover both cases.

findings.title: Error challenge no longer keeps passkeys after a failed username lookup
findings.body: `challenge(context, error, field)` used to fill the WebAuthn form data when `context.getUser() == null`. For example, after a failed username lookup, `testInvalidUser` clears the user and the form is re-rendered. It now fills the data only when a user is set, so the error page for an invalid username or password loses the passkey/conditional-UI setup. `PasskeysUsernameFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` still expects 'username webauthn' autocomplete after an invalid-user error, and that assertion would fail.

findings.title: shouldDisplayAuthenticators still keyed on user != null while authenticators are never provided
findings.body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` is overridden to return false, so `ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS` is never set for conditional UI. `shouldDisplayAuthenticators` in the base class still returns `context.getUser() != null`. During re-authentication, when a user is set, the form therefore gets `SHOULD_DISPLAY_AUTHENTICATORS=true` with no authenticator list. This is inconsistent and relies on the template tolerating the missing attribute. Override `shouldDisplayAuthenticators` consistently. The new override also lacks `@Override`, so a signature drift in the parent would go unnoticed.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey does not test a user without a passkey
findings.body: The comment and method name say the test covers a user who has no passkey, but the test only disables passkeys at the realm level with `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)`. It therefore never exercises the scenario where passkeys are enabled for the realm and the re-authenticating user has no registered passkey. In that case the conditional UI would still be offered, which is the interesting behaviour of this change. The test name and comment are misleading, and the intended case is untested.

findings.title: UsernameForm re-authentication shows a form with no usable input for users without passkeys
findings.body: When passkeys are enabled in the realm, the username-only form no longer skips itself during re-authentication, whether or not the current user has any passkey. `UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate` sets `USERNAME_HIDDEN` for the re-authenticating user. A user with no registered passkey is then shown a username page with no visible username field and no passkey to use, and must click through it before reaching the password step. The decision should depend on whether the user actually has a passkey credential, not just on the realm flag.
